messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high KV-cache memory growth on hosted-runtime pool 'eu-central-1a' - OOMs observed on 12/32 workers. Trigger: continuous-batching hit >1.5M KV entries. Incident ID 2029-CTX-42
Marta (oncall): I'm on it. pulling logs and scale targets now.
Kevin SRE: thanks — can you confirm impact? are user requests failing or just latency?
Marta (oncall): ~40% of requests returning 503s from affected hosts, big tail latency increase for streaming (p50 unchanged). Affected customers: three midmarket tenants reported errors (Ruth to confirm names).
Ruth (support): confirmed CS ticket for customer acme-analytics (prod) and an alert from beta-shop. Both saw spikes of 5xx and reconnects.
Samir (runtime): hypothesis: a client is sending very long single-turn prompts with streaming + disabled batching backpressure flag, causing KV-window to inflate because we never cut off prefix accumulation. We also recently rolled a batching helper that relaxes window caps for throughput — could be regression.
Jess (prod-eng): timeline — did we change any eviction/kv cache caps in last 24h?
Marta (oncall): deploy history shows rollout 2098761200: "continuous-batch: disable_strict_window_caps=true" to reduce latency for short chats. That matches.
Kevin SRE: ok isolate — can we cordon the pool and add a routing rule to avoid sending new streams to eu-central-1a?
Samir (runtime): quick mitigation options: 1) enable strict window caps (rollback flag) 2) apply per-request max_tokens enforcement at gateway 3) throttle streaming on affected hosts 4) restart affected workers (quick but noisy). Best low-risk: flip flag back to true and requeue new requests elsewhere.
Marta (oncall): flipping flag now in feature flags service. Command I used: 
```
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags/continuous-batch -d '{"disable_strict_window_caps":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
```
ops-automation: feature flag change deployed to eu-central-1 in 12s, config UUID ff-cc-2098.
incident-bot: change recorded — rollout id ff-cc-2098, applied to pool eu-central-1a.
Marta (oncall): observing memory graphs... KV-cache growth slope reduced within 30s on 8/12 hosts. A few hosts still climbing — likely eviction backlog.
Kevin SRE: start draining remaining climbing hosts. Add routing rule to divert new sessions off cluster and spin new instances in eu-central-1b.
Samir (runtime): issuing drain for instances i-0a12..i-0a1f. Using command: 
```
./infractl drain-host --id i-0a12..i-0a1f --grace 30
```
Jess (prod-eng): can we temporarily enforce a hard token cap per request at the API gateway to block abusive single-turn inputs until we patch client behavior?
Marta (oncall): applying 100k token soft cap now (will 429 if exceed).
ops-automation: gateway rule applied, rule id gw-ctx-2098.
Ruth (support): emailed affected customers, put a post on status page indicating degraded streaming in eu-central. Customers asked for ETA.
Marta (oncall): current status: 9/12 affected hosts stable, 3 draining/restarting. Error rate down from 35%->6% in last 6 minutes. No data loss; some streaming sessions aborted mid-stream — we should offer reconnect guidance.
Samir (runtime): root cause notes for postmortem: combination of (a) relaxed window cap rollout + (b) client long single-turn prompts with streaming that keep appending prefix tokens without trimming + (c) continuous-batching not enforcing eviction fast enough under this access pattern -> KV cache explosion -> OOM.
Kevin SRE: next steps — rollback rollout fully for global pool, add a canary with stricter metrics, and add a loaded e2e test with long single-turn streaming to catch this pattern.
Jess (prod-eng): I'll file a runbook change: require canary for any flag that changes window/ejection semantics and add kill-switch in control plane.
Marta (oncall): handing off to Kevin for full recovery and postmortem. I'll stay on until stabilization.
Kevin SRE: taking over. Current ETA for full recovery 20m to rotate cluster and validate roaming routing rule.
incident-bot: oncall handoff logged from Marta -> Kevin at ts 2098765450.
Marta (oncall): notes for handoff: customers impacted (acme-analytics, beta-shop, sku-inc), mitigation performed: rollback flag ff-cc-2098, gateway token cap gw-ctx-2098, drained hosts i-0a12..i-0a1f, restart rolling. Observed side effects: some streams aborted, increased 429s for very long requests.
Kevin SRE: accepted. I'll coordinate postmortem owner and schedule follow-up with runtime and product. Assigning PM/owner: Jess.
Jess (prod-eng): acknowledged. I'll draft postmortem and remediation plan: add per-tenant streaming token limits, strengthen eviction heuristics in continuous-batching, and require telemetry for cumulative KV entries per session.
Ruth (support): I'll update the affected customer tickets with the mitigation steps and offer guidance for reconnect and trimming prompts.
Samir (runtime): quick patch to enforce eviction fastpath queued (PR 3421), target merge after tests.
Kevin SRE: final check — error rates stable ~<1% on new routing, memory normalizing. Closing pager in 30m unless regress.
incident-bot: Incident 2029-CTX-42 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
Marta (oncall): leaving final note: don't merge any continuous-batch window relax changes without a canary. Handing off slack thread to postmortem channel after stabilization. Thanks all :heart:
